what_its_for: Baricitinib is used to treat moderate to severe rheumatoid arthritis (joint pain and swelling caused by your immune system attacking your joints) in adults when other medicines have not worked well enough. It may also be used for alopecia areata (a condition that causes hair loss) and, in some cases, COVID-19 in hospitalized patients. It works by blocking certain proteins in your body that cause inflammation.
how_to_take: Take baricitinib by mouth, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, split, or chew it. Try to take it at the same time every day so it becomes part of your routine. If you have trouble swallowing the tablet, talk to your doctor or pharmacist before changing how you take it.
dosing: The usual dose for rheumatoid arthritis is 2 mg once daily. For alopecia areata, the usual dose is 2 mg once daily, which may be increased to 4 mg once daily by your doctor. Your doctor may lower your dose if you have kidney problems or if you are taking certain other medicines. Always take the exact dose your doctor prescribed — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time. Do not take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store baricitinib at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep it away from moisture and heat — do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid being around people who are sick or have infections, as baricitinib lowers your ability to fight infections. Do not receive live vaccines (such as the shingles shot Zostavax or MMR) while taking this medicine — ask your doctor which vaccines are safe. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and use sunscreen, as this medicine may increase your risk of certain skin cancers. Limit or avoid alcohol, as it can increase side effects. Tell all your doctors and dentists that you are taking this medicine before any procedure.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: signs of serious infection such as fever, chills, sweats, cough, shortness of breath, or painful urination; chest pain or pressure; signs of a blood clot such as sudden leg pain, swelling, redness, or difficulty breathing; unusual lumps or skin changes that could suggest cancer; stomach pain, nausea, or yellowing of your skin or eyes (signs of liver problems); or any new or unusual symptoms that worry you. Call your doctor if you have any signs of allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in your joint pain and stiffness within 1 to 2 weeks of starting baricitinib. However, it may take several weeks to months to feel the full benefit of the medicine. Keep taking it even if you do not feel better right away, and do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): You may have a higher risk of serious infections, blood clots, heart problems, and certain cancers. Your doctor will weigh the benefits and risks carefully. Kidney problems: Your dose may need to be lowered if your kidneys do not work well. This medicine is not recommended if you have very severe kidney disease. Liver problems: Talk to your doctor if you have liver disease, as baricitinib may not be right for you. Pregnancy: Do not take baricitinib if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it may harm the unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 week after the last dose. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for at least 2 days after your last dose. Children: Baricitinib is approved for children 2 years and older only for alopecia areata. Use in other conditions in children has not been approved. Always tell your doctor about all your health conditions and medicines before starting baricitinib.
